items.title: Local User System With Bootstrap Admin

requirements.statement: Jido.Code shall use Jido.Runic strategy and directive machinery to connect workflow planning with Jido runtime directives and completion signals.
Jido.Code shall treat Jido.Runic as the canonical execution integration layer for repository runs and workflow-driven step orchestration.

Repository-specific prep and validation activities such as sync, dependency install, lint, tests, and spec checks shall be modeled as explicit workflow steps when they affect execution evidence or control decisions.
The durable Run resource shall be a control-plane projection around Jido.Runic-managed workflow state rather than a duplicate step engine.
Jido.Code shall treat Runic as the underlying DAG and runnable substrate beneath Jido.Runic rather than as the primary integration surface.
Generic sandbox bootstrap shall remain distinct from repository-specific prep performed inside a workflow run.
Sprite session resources shall own sandbox provisioning, generic bootstrap, checkpointing, and resume lifecycle.
Viability-threatening conditions shall support direct escalation from lower levels to higher policy levels without waiting for normal queue progression.
Jido.Code shall model the factory instance as a viable system whose primary operational units are ManagedRepo records.
Each ManagedRepo shall be treated as a recursive viable system with explicit operational, coordination, control, intelligence, and policy responsibilities.
The architecture shall define the conditions under which a lower-level work unit may be promoted into its own recursive viable subsystem.
ManagedRepo System 1 shall be expressed through operational work loops represented by WorkItem categories and executed through Run records.
WorkItem and Run shall be treated as operational records rather than full viable systems unless they are explicitly promoted through a lower-level viability rule.
When GitHub-backed automation is enabled, GitHub App mode shall be the preferred integration path over PAT fallback because it offers scoped installation access and repository-aware validation.
If GitHub-backed user sign-in is introduced, it shall resolve to a local user record and preserve the same administrator-versus-member role model used by local authentication.
Email/password and magic-link authentication shall remain available even when GitHub App configuration is absent or invalid.
Setup shall report whether GitHub App mode or PAT fallback is configured and whether repository access is confirmed for the current administrator context.
Provider-login broker configuration shall remain distinct from deployment-local GitHub automation credentials and shall not be reused as the automation credential source.
GitHub automation credentials shall use canonical deployment-local SecretRef names for GitHub App ID, GitHub App private key, GitHub webhook secret, and PAT fallback.
GitHub automation runtime callers shall resolve deployment-local credentials from environment or encrypted SecretRefs without depending on provider-login configuration state.
The Provider Login section shall let an operator persist provider-host enablement, allowlist posture, and broker trust fields without collecting Git automation secrets in the same form.
The Git Provider Integrations section shall show GitHub automation readiness feedback, including path-level validation detail and remediation, using deployment-local credential checks.

The operator console shall make the boundary explicit between provider-login broker configuration and deployment-local Git service secrets, and it shall keep GitLab and Bitbucket service integrations in explicit placeholder status.
The authenticated landing page shall present separate Provider Login and Git Provider Integrations sections.
Broker-issued handoff JWTs shall be verified against broker JWKS material before any local identity linking or session issuance is attempted.
The deployment complete endpoint shall validate signed state and broker handoff JWT before provider-specific identity linking and local session issuance are allowed to proceed.
Broker-issued handoff JWTs shall fail closed when issuer or audience does not match the provider-host configuration.
Broker-issued handoff JWTs shall bind back to the signed deployment state through a matching nonce and provider context.
Successfully validated broker handoff nonces shall be single-use so replay attempts fail closed and expiry evaluation stays consistent with the validating request clock.
The deployment start endpoint shall redirect to the configured broker start URL with signed state, provider host, and deployment callback URL.
The deployment shall issue a signed provider-auth state token that binds provider, provider host, broker base URL, redirect path, and nonce.
Signed provider-auth state shall expire after a bounded TTL and fail closed when reused after expiry.
Provider-linked identity records shall have durable schema support for authentication metadata such as first and most recent successful authentication timestamps.
External provider identities shall resolve through a local identity record that uniquely maps provider plus host plus provider subject to one local user.
The provider auth foundation shall recognize GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket as the initial provider catalog.
The system shall persist provider-host login configuration including enablement, allowlist posture, and broker trust fields without coupling it to provider automation secrets.
Provider-linked identity records shall store the first and most recent successful provider authentication timestamps.
When no linked identity exists and no existing local user matches by verified provider email, the system shall provision a local user record from provider identity data.
When a provider plus host plus subject identity already exists, the system shall reuse that linked local user instead of creating a second local account.
When no provider identity exists but the provider email is verified and matches an existing local user, the system shall attach the provider identity to that local user.
Provider sign-in shall consume broker-validated provider claims only after the deployment-side state and broker handoff contract has already been validated.
The landing page shall expose a GitHub provider sign-in entrypoint when GitHub.com provider login is enabled.
Local email sign-in and account-creation entrypoints shall remain visible even when provider login is unavailable or disabled.
Successful provider sign-in shall issue the same revocable local browser session credential used by local authentication.
Successful provider sign-in shall resolve to the existing local user model through provider-identity linking before a browser session is issued.
The local session-issuance service for provider sign-in shall remain provider-neutral so additional VCS identity providers can reuse the same token and local-user model.
After successful provider sign-in, the browser shall redirect to the signed deployment redirect path rather than stopping at an intermediate contract response.
Provider login shall evaluate the configured allowlist mode and values before local user linking proceeds.
Provider identities that fail login policy shall be rejected before the system creates or links a local user.
Provider login shall respect per-provider and per-host enablement flags before allowing login resolution.
Allowlist evaluation shall remain provider-neutral so users, organizations, teams, groups, and workspaces can be evaluated through the same policy contract.
Provider-login allowlist rejection shall block provider session issuance without breaking deployment-local GitHub automation validation.
Local email authentication shall remain available when broker validation is unavailable or fails for provider login.
A self-hosted deployment shall support broker-backed GitHub login while deployment-local GitHub automation validation is simultaneously ready.
GitHub automation validation shall remain available even when browser provider login is disabled for that provider host.
New email-backed identities shall support confirmation tracking before they are treated as confirmed accounts.
Authentication shall be anchored to a local user record with a unique email identity.
Local authentication shall support email magic-link sign-in and registration.
Local authentication shall support email-and-password registration and sign-in with password confirmation and minimum-length validation.
Local authentication shall support forgot-password recovery by issuing a reset token and allowing token-based password reset.
The system shall persist session credentials and API keys so they can be listed and revoked as part of account security operations.
The landing page shall present local authentication entrypoints for anonymous users, an enabled provider-login entrypoint when configured, and a sign-out control for authenticated users.
Authenticated product routes and deployment integration routes shall remain declared in the router rather than being commented out or silently disabled.
The browser route surface shall keep `/`, `/welcome`, `/setup`, and authentication entrypoints available as the public operator entry surface.
The root path shall redirect to `/welcome` so the operator-facing landing route stays canonical even as authenticated product routes expand.
The welcome landing page shall present the copy "Welcome to Jido Code" and act as the operator-facing starting point for sign-in and setup.
The repository shall instruct agents to run bw prime before starting work and use Beadwork for durable local work state.
The repository shall prefer GitHub issues and pull requests for non-trivial collaboration and shall avoid landing changes directly on main.
The operator guide shall explain the callback, redirect, signed-state, and allowlist flow for self-hosted provider login.
The operator guide shall explain the current future-provider posture for GitLab and Bitbucket so operators do not assume those integrations are production-ready yet.
The operator guide shall describe the exact GitHub login app registration fields used for the broker-managed login model.
The operator guide shall describe deployment-local GitHub service credential setup, including canonical SecretRef names and supported environment variables.
The repository shall publish a first data ontology that defines the preferred control-plane record names, their relationships, and the initial Ash resource framing.
The repository shall expose the foundation docs through both docs/README.md and the top-level README documentation section.
The repository shall publish a Jido-centric product comparison note that captures what Jido.Code should learn from Factory.ai and where it should deliberately differentiate.
The repository shall publish a technical implementation document that states the technical stance, the durable control loop, and the intended Ash domain layout.
The repository shall publish a vision document that states the core product idea, what Jido.Code is building, the trust model, and the initial scope.
Auth-provider foundation work shall be specified and implemented inside jido_code rather than split into a separate product repo.
The jido_code repository shall serve as the primary product and implementation repo for active work in this workspace.
The repository shall maintain a package-local .spec workspace for current-truth subject specs, durable ADRs, and generated spec state.
Contributor-facing quality, CI, release, and spec-alignment surfaces shall live in version-controlled repo files instead of ad hoc local state.
The repository shall keep a repo-local comparison document that maps jido_code to the canonical Jido package quality standards and records any explicit product-repo exceptions.
The repository shall keep version-controlled CI and release workflows that enforce the documented package quality baseline for this repo.
Any repo-specific deviation from the canonical package standards shall be explicit and documented instead of remaining implicit drift.
The repository shall provide a standards-aligned mix quality surface with coverage metadata, a `mix q` shortcut, and quality checks that include format, compile warnings, Credo, Dialyzer, and Doctor.
The repository shall include the contributor-facing root files required by the package quality standards: README, CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS, LICENSE, and usage-rules.
Source provider adapters shall implement a shared behavior for configuration, service credential resolution, API token lookup, and repository listing.
GitHub service credential checks shall delegate provider-specific credential and repository-access logic through the GitHub adapter rather than reaching directly into GitHub modules.
The GitHub adapter shall preserve GitHub App preference ahead of PAT fallback in the setup-path model.
GitLab and Bitbucket shall have explicit placeholder adapters so unsupported provider integrations fail through named boundaries rather than implicit missing-module behavior.
The source provider boundary shall enumerate GitHub, GitLab, and Bitbucket adapter modules through a shared provider catalog.
The repository shall include a .spec/AGENTS.md that gives local operating guidance for agents working inside the .spec workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/decisions/README.md that explains when durable ADRs belong in the workspace.
The repository shall include a .spec/README.md that explains purpose, layout, and workflow.
When planning and verification run, the workspace shall generate .spec/state.json containing indexed subjects, indexed decisions, and verification state.
Administrators shall be able to add users and initiate account creation without reopening unrestricted public registration.
The system shall identify which users are administrators so policy, auditing, and management actions can resolve the acting admin explicitly.
Initial setup shall create or confirm exactly one bootstrap administrator before admin-managed account features are used.
The account model shall treat administrators and standard members as users in one local user system rather than separate identity silos.
Once the bootstrap administrator exists in production, open self-registration shall remain gated unless an administrator explicitly provisions or invites the account.
Both administrators and standard users shall be able to sign in, sign out, and complete forgot-password recovery for their own accounts.

given: A run starts in a fresh sprite with no active workspace state.
then: Session bootstrap handles sandbox setup first, and repository prep remains explicit workflow work inside the run.
when: The system prepares execution for repository work.

given: A managed repository launches a new run for a work item.
then: Jido.Runic drives execution, Runic provides the underlying workflow mechanics, and the Ash Run record reflects the resulting control-plane state.
when: The run advances through planning and execution.

given: A run reaches repository validation after implementation or repair work.
then: They may be represented as explicit workflow steps that fan out and rejoin before the next approval or landing decision.
when: Lint, tests, and spec checks can execute independently.

given: The factory is supervising multiple managed repositories.
then: ManagedRepo units are treated as the factory's operational subsystems rather than as unrelated records.
when: Operators reason about capacity, policy, and cross-repo demand.

given: A managed repository receives new demand from intake or observation.
then: WorkItem and Run operate inside the repo's System 1 scope while coordination, control, and policy remain explicit at the repo level.
when: The repository orchestrator assesses that demand and creates work.

given: A viability-threatening condition appears inside a managed repository.
then: The condition can bypass the normal queue and escalate directly to higher policy authority.
when: Normal queue processing would be too slow or too noisy to preserve control.

given: A single work item or run is created for routine repository work.
then: The work packet remains an operational record unless it has persistent identity, bounded mission, its own coordination needs, its own feedback loop, and distinct policy constraints.
when: The architecture classifies its control scope.

given: GitHub App credentials are configured and the installation can access the expected repositories.
then: The system reports GitHub App mode as ready for the current administrator context.
when: Setup validates GitHub integration.

given: A future GitHub-backed sign-in flow is enabled.
then: The system links that identity to a local user record before authorization decisions are made.
when: A GitHub identity authenticates successfully.

given: GitHub App credentials are not configured and PAT validation succeeds.
then: The system reports PAT fallback readiness without blocking local user authentication flows.
when: Setup validates GitHub integration.

given: A deployment-local GitHub automation secret exists in encrypted SecretRefs.
The same credential is also present in root environment configuration.
then: The root environment value wins and the secret-ref metadata remains non-authoritative for that resolution.
when: GitHub automation resolves that credential.

given: Provider-login configuration is stored in the provider config model.
then: The automation model names deployment-local service secrets separately from provider-login broker fields.
when: GitHub automation service credentials are described for setup and runtime callers.

given: A deployment-local GitHub automation secret is absent from runtime env and present in encrypted SecretRefs under its canonical name.
then: The encrypted SecretRef value is used.
when: GitHub automation resolves that credential.

given: GitHub automation depends on deployment-local credentials.
then: The page renders path-level readiness and remediation feedback separately from provider-login settings.
when: The operator refreshes GitHub integration validation.

given: A local operator needs to enable hosted provider login.
then: The provider config persists broker trust and allowlist fields without storing Git automation secrets.
when: The operator saves provider-host login settings on the landing page.

given: A local operator is already signed in on the baseline landing page.
then: The page shows separate Provider Login and Git Provider Integrations sections and keeps future provider integrations explicit.
when: The operator opens the landing page.

given: A provider-host config has broker trust fields.
then: Start redirects to the broker contract URL, and complete validates the broker contract before any local provider sign-in work runs.
when: The deployment start and complete endpoints are invoked.

given: A broker returns a signed handoff JWT.
then: Invalid issuer, audience, expiry, or replay attempts fail closed.
when: The deployment validates that JWT against broker trust settings and the signed state nonce.

given: A deployment operator starts provider sign-in for a configured provider host.
then: The provider state round-trips with the same nonce and fails once it expires.
when: The deployment issues and later verifies the provider-auth state token.

given: A local user already exists.
then: Future provider lookups can resolve the same local user through the provider plus host plus subject tuple and keep provider-auth metadata on the identity record.
when: The system records a provider identity for that user.

given: An operator needs to prepare hosted provider login.
then: The system persists provider-neutral login settings without storing automation credentials in the same record.
when: The operator saves provider-host configuration for an approved source provider.

given: No linked provider identity exists and the verified provider email is not yet present in the local directory.
then: The system provisions one local user and future verified identities for the same email attach back to that user.
when: The provider identity authenticates.

given: A provider identity is already linked to a local user.
then: The same local user is returned and the most recent authentication timestamp is refreshed without losing the original first-authenticated timestamp.
when: The same provider identity authenticates again.

given: A local user exists without a provider identity.
then: The provider identity attaches to that local user instead of creating a duplicate user.
when: A provider identity with the same verified email authenticates.

given: GitHub.com provider login has been enabled for the deployment.
then: The page shows both local auth entrypoints and the GitHub sign-in entrypoint.
when: An anonymous visitor opens the landing page.

given: The deployment has already validated broker state and handoff claims for a GitHub identity.
then: The flow links or provisions the local user, issues a revocable session token, and redirects the browser to the signed redirect path.
when: The provider sign-in service consumes those claims.

given: A provider identity does not satisfy the configured allowlist.
then: The identity is rejected before a local user is created or linked.
when: Login is attempted.

given: A provider host is configured with an allowlist.
then: The login is allowed to proceed into local identity linking.
when: Provider identity facts match the configured allowlist values.

given: A provider host is configured but login is disabled.
then: The login is rejected before local user linking begins.
when: A provider identity attempts login.

given: Provider login is enabled and restricted by an allowlist.
Deployment-local GitHub automation credentials remain configured.
then: Provider login is rejected and GitHub automation readiness still renders for the local operator path.
when: A provider identity outside the allowlist attempts sign-in.

given: Provider login is enabled for GitHub.com.
Broker trust validation is unavailable.
then: Local email sign-in and account access remain available.
when: Provider sign-in fails.

given: Provider login is enabled for GitHub.com.
Deployment-local GitHub App credentials are configured.
then: The local session is issued and the authenticated landing page shows GitHub automation as ready.
when: A broker-validated GitHub identity completes sign-in.

given: Browser provider login is disabled for GitHub.com.
Deployment-local GitHub automation credentials remain configured.
then: Provider login stays disabled while GitHub automation readiness remains available.
when: An operator inspects the authenticated landing page.

given: A user prefers passwordless access.
then: The system signs in the existing user or creates the local user identity allowed by policy.
when: The user requests and consumes a valid magic link.

given: A user has forgotten their password.
then: The password is changed and the user can authenticate with the new secret.
when: The user requests reset instructions and completes the reset flow with a valid token.

given: A user has a local email identity and a valid password.
then: The system issues a revocable authenticated session token.
when: The user signs in through the password flow.

given: An operator is evaluating GitLab and Bitbucket.
then: The guide makes it clear that those providers are modeled but not operator-ready end to end yet.
when: The operator reads the provider auth guide.

given: An operator needs to enable hosted GitHub login for a self-hosted deployment.
then: The guide explains the broker-managed callback model and the exact deployment-side fields to configure.
when: The operator reads the provider auth guide.

given: An operator needs GitHub automation to work in the same deployment.
then: The guide lists the deployment-local secrets, env vars, and readiness expectations without mixing them into broker login config.
when: The operator reads the provider auth guide.

given: A contributor starts from the docs index or the repository README.
then: The vision, technical implementation, and data ontology docs are linked directly.
when: The contributor looks for foundational product documentation.

given: A contributor wants to understand what Jido.Code is trying to build before editing implementation code.
then: The docs explain the product thesis, the technical stance, the base control-plane model, and how Jido.Code should position itself relative to adjacent agent-development products without requiring code spelunking.
when: The contributor reads the foundation docs.

given: Setup needs to validate deployment-local GitHub service credentials.
then: The checks call the GitHub adapter boundary and keep GitHub App ahead of PAT fallback.
when: GitHub credential checks enumerate credential paths and request accessible repositories.

given: Future GitLab and Bitbucket integration is not implemented yet.
then: The registry resolves named placeholder adapters for those providers.
when: The source provider registry is queried.

given: A bootstrap administrator is signed in.
then: The new account enters the local user system without reopening unrestricted public sign-up.
when: The administrator provisions a new team member account.

given: The deployment has no existing users.
then: The system establishes one bootstrap administrator who becomes the first accountable local user.
when: Initial setup is completed.

given: A standard user account exists in the local directory.
then: The user completes self-service recovery without requiring direct administrator password handling.
when: The user forgets their password.

meta.summary: jido_code authenticates local users with email-backed identities, password and magic-link flows, confirmation, and revocable session credentials backed by persisted security-token surfaces.
jido_code exposes a welcome landing page and auth entrypoints at the public edge while keeping authenticated product, RPC, API, and dev surfaces declared in the router.
jido_code uses Beadwork for local durable agent state and GitHub issues plus pull requests for shared collaboration.

Jido.Code centers execution on Jido.Runic, which drives Runic workflows through the Jido runtime while sprite sessions provide sandbox lifecycle and Ash resources provide durable governance projections.
jido_code keeps local user accounts as the source of truth while supporting GitHub App and PAT integration, synchronizing installation readiness, and preparing for optional GitHub-backed sign-in.
jido_code keeps GitHub automation credentials deployment-local, names them through canonical SecretRefs, and does not reuse provider-login broker configuration for automation.

authenticated operators can manage provider-login broker trust on the landing page, see GitHub automation readiness separately, and keep Git service secrets distinct from provider-login configuration.

jido_code publishes an operator guide that explains broker-managed GitHub login, deployment-local GitHub service credentials, callback and allowlist behavior, and future GitLab or Bitbucket posture without requiring operators to read implementation code.

jido_code is the primary implementation repo, maintains a package-local Spec Led workspace, keeps contributor-facing quality surfaces version-controlled, and evolves auth-provider foundation, linking, login-policy, and GitHub service-credential work inside that repo.
jido_code keeps the contributor-facing quality surfaces from the Jido package standards current while documenting explicit product-repo exceptions.

Jido.Code publishes a concise vision doc, a terse technical implementation doc, a first data ontology doc, and repository-level doc indexes that point operators and contributors to those foundational materials.
jido_code persists provider-backed user identities and provider login configuration without replacing the local user system.

jido_code signs deployment-owned provider state, validates broker JWT handoffs with issuer and audience trust, blocks nonce replay with a consistent request clock, and enforces the contract that must pass before provider-specific local sign-in can proceed.
jido_code resolves provider identities to local users by reusing an existing identity, linking verified email addresses, or provisioning a new local user when needed.

jido_code exposes a GitHub provider sign-in entrypoint, consumes broker-validated provider claims, links them to the local user system, and issues the same revocable local session tokens used by email sign-in before redirecting back to the signed landing path.
jido_code evaluates provider login enablement and provider-neutral allowlists before allowing provider identities to resolve into local users.

jido_code makes self-hosted provider login behavior explicit by testing broker-backed GitHub login, deployment-local GitHub automation readiness, disabled-login separation, broker failure fallback, and allowlist rejection against the `/welcome` landing flow.
jido_code routes GitHub service credential and repository-access checks through a provider-neutral adapter boundary and keeps explicit placeholder adapters for GitLab and Bitbucket.
Canonical workspace contract for authored specs and generated Spec Led state.
jido_code boots with an initial administrator through the welcome/setup path and grows into an admin-managed multi-user account system with guarded registration.

Jido.Code models the factory instance and each ManagedRepo as recursive viable systems, while treating WorkItem and Run as operational records unless explicitly promoted to lower-level viable subsystems.
